skill.name: wireshark-analysis
skill.description: Guides Wireshark packet capture, filtering, stream reconstruction, and network investigation workflows for troubleshooting and security analysis.
skill.summary: Analyze PCAP files and live captures with structured Wireshark workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and Wireshark filter examples. I confirmed the private-key handling risk and added a semantic finding for credential exposure workflows in packet analysis. No prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace broad private-key instructions with authorized key-handling steps. Keep keys outside AI chats, protect temporary key logs, and document secure disposal.
Add explicit authorization, scoping, redaction, retention, and reporting guidance before any credential search or HTTP object export.

remediation.issue: Audit noise from unlabeled fenced examples
remediation.suggestion: Label non-executable Markdown fences as text or wireshark-filter so scanners do not treat fence markers as shell execution.

content.value_statement: Network packet captures can be hard to filter and explain. This skill provides Wireshark workflows for capture setup, filters, stream review, statistics, and incident notes.
actual_capabilities: Guides live capture setup and interface selection in Wireshark.
Provides capture filter and display filter examples for common protocols.
Explains how to follow TCP, UDP, HTTP, and TLS streams.
Uses Wireshark statistics views to review conversations, endpoints, flows, and traffic rates.
Supports security investigations for scans, suspicious DNS, malware traffic, and plaintext credentials.
Lists troubleshooting steps for capture permissions, filter errors, and performance issues.
limitations: Requires Wireshark and local permission to capture or inspect traffic.
Cannot decrypt modern TLS without lawful access to approved key material.
Does not replace incident response procedures, legal review, or privacy policy checks.
Very large captures may require sampling, splitting, or specialized hardware.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Slow Applications
use_cases.description: Find retransmissions, latency, DNS failures, and response-time patterns in a capture.

use_cases.title: Investigate Security Incidents
use_cases.description: Review suspicious hosts, command and control patterns, unusual DNS, and plaintext credential exposure.

use_cases.title: Teach Packet Analysis
use_cases.description: Use structured filters, stream views, and statistics to explain protocol behavior from real captures.

prompt_templates.title: Review a PCAP
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a known capture file.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a PCAP from a slow web application. Help me inspect it in Wireshark for latency, retransmissions, DNS errors, and failed connections.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized Wireshark capture for one host and one service. Include capture scope, filters, privacy precautions, and what evidence to record.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Suspicious Host
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through Wireshark analysis for a suspected compromised host. Focus on DNS patterns, unusual ports, beaconing, and traffic leaving the trusted network.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Incident Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn Wireshark observations into an incident evidence summary. Include timeline, endpoints, protocols, notable streams, uncertainty, and redaction needs.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to analyze a PCAP for slow web traffic.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests filtering to the web server, checking retransmissions, reviewing service response times, and comparing packet rates in an I/O graph.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to investigate suspicious DNS activity.
output_examples.output: The skill guides the user to isolate DNS queries, separate responses from requests, review failed lookups, and document unusual query names.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to check for plaintext credential exposure.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends authorized scope first, then stream review, HTTP form inspection, and careful redaction of any discovered sensitive data.

best_practices: Confirm authorization and minimize capture scope before collecting traffic.
Use capture filters first, then display filters to narrow analysis safely.
Protect PCAP files and redact secrets before sharing findings.
anti_patterns: Capturing broad network traffic when a host or service filter is enough.
Uploading raw PCAPs that may contain credentials or private content.
Declaring an endpoint malicious without corroborating timing, protocol, and context evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill run Wireshark automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis workflows and filter guidance for a user operating Wireshark.

faq.question: Can it analyze live traffic?
faq.answer: Yes, when the user has Wireshark installed and authorization to capture on the selected interface.

faq.question: Can it decrypt TLS traffic?
faq.answer: Only when the user has lawful access to approved key material or browser key logs.

faq.question: Is it suitable for incident response?
faq.answer: It can support packet-level investigation, but it does not replace incident response procedures.

faq.question: Does it include safe handling guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It advises authorized capture, privacy-aware handling, and protection of sensitive PCAP files.

faq.question: What files does this skill include?
faq.answer: The skill contains a single SKILL.md file with Wireshark workflows, filters, examples, and troubleshooting notes.
